newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar stays weakness, movements tight.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar stays weakness, movements tight.

text.p: London's white sugar futures market was content to follow a similar pattern to the morning as movements on both spreads and premiums remained tight before New York's March raws expiry.
Earlier trade and broker selling drove the spot May contract down to a low of $304.00, with the bearish sentiment dragging down the further forward months.
May/August hovered between premium and discount as May weakened in a continued technical reaction to last week's strength.
Traders said they expected the spread to narrow to a discount as buying had been noted at 50 cents under par.
At 1645 GMT May was down $1.10 at $305.00 and August down 70 cents at $305.00. Volume was dominated by the two front months and totalled 1,374 lots.
"It is very quiet, the movements are very tight," said one trader.
Limited activity was reported on the white premium and was mainly a function of more volatile trading in New York before the March expiry at the end of the week.
"New York has been moving and London hasn't -- and next morning London gets sold down to pull it back into line," another trader said.

Technically, the outlook for May whites is gradually turning May is drifting lower towards $303.00, a 50-percent Fibonacci retracement point based on the rally from last month's $293.50 trough up to last week's high of $312.50.
While the position has managed to hold above an upward trendline dating from the January trough, a fall beneath the line would confirm this week's breakdown in sentiment, analysts said.
In physical news, Iraq has postponed its tender to buy sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal until February 28 but the quantity required is still unclear.
Syria tenders on Wednesday to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws, both amounts for April shipment. Results are to be made known on Thursday.
Paris values also moved lower but volume was much smaller than in London at just 338 lots.
May was down 70 cents at $304.60 and August down 60 cents at $304.50.
